profile.summary: FlowDock predicts the three dimensional structure of a protein-ligand complex and, at the same time, how strongly the ligand binds. The inputs are protein sequences and ligand SMILES strings, with no pocket and no multiple sequence alignment needed; the model first predicts an unbound protein structure with ESMFold, then moves it towards a bound structure. Each generated complex comes with a structural confidence score and a binding affinity value, and several ligands can be modelled at the same time.

summary_quotes.text: accepts both (multi-chain) protein sequences and (multi-fragment) ligand SMILES strings as its primary inputs, which it uses to predict an unbound (apo) state of the protein sequences using ESMFold
runs confidence and binding affinity heads to predict structural confidence scores (i.e. plDDT) and binding affinities of the predicted complex structure, to rank-order the model’s generated samples.
**FlowDock: Geometric Flow Matching for Generative Protein-Ligand Docking and Affinity Prediction**

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: FlowDock is a conditional flow matching model: it learns a path from an unbound (apo) protein structure to the bound (holo) structure, for any number of binding ligands. The protein side starts from an ESMFold structure, which the authors use as a surrogate prior, and the ligand side starts from a harmonic prior constrained by the bond graph of the given SMILES string. The network is the NeuralPLexer architecture, which encodes protein language model sequence embeddings and ligand SMILES strings and decodes contact maps that condition a flow ordinary differential equation for the coordinates. The authors fine-tune NeuralPLexer's score head with the flow matching objective, along with its other intermediate weights and heads, including a confidence head redesigned to predict binding affinity; NeuralPLexer's original confidence head stays frozen.

quotes.text: the first deep geometric generative model based on conditional flow matching (CFM) that learns to directly map unbound (apo) structures to their bound (holo) counterparts for an arbitrary number of binding ligands

sections.title: Training data and compute
sections.body: Training used PDBBind-E, which the authors describe as an enhanced version of a PDBBind 2020 based training set: they collected 17 743 crystal complex structures from PDBBind 2020 and 47 183 structures from the Binding MOAD. The repository also ships preparation steps for DockGen and a PDB based van der Mers dataset, and a fine-tuning route on PLINDER, which it warns needs about an hour to download and about 750G of storage. The paper states that FlowDock was trained using only 4 80GB H100 GPUs for 1 week, which it contrasts with the 128 A100 GPUs for one month it attributes to Chai-1.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The published weights are a tar archive on Zenodo record 15066450, and the commands in the README name two checkpoints from it: esmfold_prior_paper_weights.ckpt for fine-tuning and esmfold_prior_paper_weights-EMA.ckpt for evaluation and sampling. The pretrained NeuralPLexer weights are a separate download, from Zenodo record 10373581. A result should name the checkpoint, the prior type, the sampler and the number of steps, since those are all command line settings; the README's examples use prior_type=esmfold, sampler=VDODE, num_steps=40 and n_samples=5. The repository also ships a Dockerfile and points at a prebuilt image.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: The NeuralPLexer architecture, fine-tuned with a flow matching objective: protein language model sequence embeddings and ligand SMILES are encoded, block diagonal contact maps are decoded to condition a flow ODE on the coordinates, and separate confidence and affinity heads score each sample.

quotes.text: with the NeuralPLexer model which encodes protein language model (PLM) sequence embeddings and ligand SMILES strings to iteratively decode block diagonal contact maps to condition a flow ODE for equivariant coordinates and auxiliary predictions.
runs confidence and binding affinity heads to predict structural confidence scores (i.e. plDDT) and binding affinities of the predicted complex structure, to rank-order the model’s generated samples.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: Protein sequences, which may be multi-chain, and ligand SMILES strings, which may be multi-fragment and are delimited by a vertical bar for several ligands. A template protein structure is optional: with input_template=null the script predicts the ESMFold structure first. A csv file can be given instead for batched prediction.

gaps: No parameter count is given in the sources read.
No inference hardware or memory requirement is stated as a number; the paper mentions a runtime and peak memory table for a subset of the Astex Diverse dataset, which was not transcribed here.
The licence of the Zenodo checkpoint archive and of the preprocessed datasets was not checked: the Zenodo records themselves were not fetched.
The reported accuracy figures are not transcribed here beyond the two the paper states in prose about docking success rate.

run_guide.summary: Install the environment, download the FlowDock and NeuralPLexer weights, and sample complex structures with affinities for one protein sequence and one ligand SMILES string.
prerequisites: Mamba or conda, and the environment file environments/flowdock_environment.yaml from the repository.
A CUDA GPU: the sampling and evaluation commands in the README are given with trainer=gpu.
Disk space for two weight downloads, the FlowDock checkpoints from Zenodo record 15066450 and the pretrained NeuralPLexer weights from Zenodo record 10373581.
The code is MIT licensed. The sources read do not state a licence for the Zenodo weight archives.

git clone https://github.com/BioinfoMachineLearning/FlowDock
cd FlowDock

conda activate FlowDock

notes: The record comes from the Wang and Cheng 2026 leakage-controlled benchmark preprint, which is on bioRxiv only (pdf at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.09.17.752433v1.full.pdf) and was not fetched in this pass, so nothing here is taken from it. Name collision worth noting: Europe PMC also lists a different model called FlowDock, 'A unified flow-based framework for flexible protein-ligand docking and binding affinity prediction' (doi 10.1016/j.apsb.2026.04.009), by other authors. This page describes Morehead and Cheng's FlowDock, the one whose repository and ISMB 2025 paper match the record description (ESMFold and NeuralPLexer components). The Zenodo records holding the weights and preprocessed data were not fetched, so no licence is claimed for them.
